answer: An agent economy can anchor each agent to one verified identity and require a deposit that stays locked while the agent trades. A single operator who wants a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred deposits, and bad behavior burns the deposit. The tide of cheap copies stops there, because copies cost real money instead of a few lines of code. Yarrow spreads in a garden only where someone planted and watered it; a sybil swarm should face the same friction, with each new identity demanding its own deposit.
